name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>; descriptor 'mark_char_as_dead' accurately reflects the action (sets the runtime-char flags byte to dead). No Ghidra address residue.
purpose: Mark a runtime character (by array index) as dead by writing its flags byte = 1.
logic_summary: Computes runtime_char[char_idx] via base pointer data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr plus char_idx * 0x50 (RUNTIME_CHAR_SIZE), then writes byte 0x1 to the entry's flags field at struct offset +5. Overwrites the whole byte, so all other flag bits are reset; bit 0 = dead is the only convention used at runtime. Leading PUSH 4 / CALL is the Watcom __CHK stack-overflow guard (4-byte frame), not game logic. No return value.

params.name: char_idx
params.semantics: Index into the runtime character array (data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr); selects which char's flags byte (offset +5) is set to dead.
params.reason: Descriptive and matches body usage as the runtime_char array index; no address residue.

notes: Disassembly verified: EAX = char_idx*5 then <<4 = char_idx*0x50 (stride 0x50 = runtime char entry size); MOV byte [base+EAX+0x5],0x1 -> flags at offset +5 = CHARFLAG_DEAD (1). src comment ('Set runtime_char[char_idx].flags = 1 (dead). Overwrites all bits.') is already concise and correct -> keep. Ghidra plate is more detailed (caller list, __CHK note) but consistent with src and not stale -> leave untouched. writes_globals empty: the write targets a heap entry reached through the global pointer, not a static global. 6 callers: mid-battle kill (fd2_enemy_turn_action_dispatcher) and story-driven chapter death marking (chapters 01/23/28 init, 23 end, event handler 17).
